justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Video Consultation Service handles consultations (R-01), E-Prescription Integration Container handles regional prescriptions (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Container provides triage recommendations (R-03), and Patient Consent & Profile Container with Consent Cryptography Service manages granular consent (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is achieved through Mediasoup WebRTC SFU, Bandwidth Adaptability Controller with Simulcast/SVC, GPU node pools in PyTorch Inference Core, Memorystore Redis caching, and asynchronous processing via Google Cloud Pub/Sub and the Outbox Pattern.
justifications.compatibility: R-08 is directly addressed by US Pharmacy Network Adapter implementing HL7 FHIR over HTTPS and EU National Gateway Adapter supporting national formats with pinned mTLS, alongside Identity Providers using OAuth 2.0/OIDC.
justifications.usability: Users (Patients, Clinicians, Compliance Officer) access appropriate capabilities via API Gateway / Ingress supporting FIDO2/WebAuthn. However, client-side frontends (mobile or web applications) for rural patients and clinicians are not modeled as containers.
justifications.reliability: R-06 is explicitly addressed by Bandwidth Adaptability Controller dynamically tuning Simulcast/SVC layers for sub-300 kbit/s connections. Fault tolerance is bolstered by Resilience & Fallback Middleware, Outbox Pattern / Reliability Component, and Pub/Sub Dead-Letter Queues.
justifications.security: Addresses GDPR/HIPAA with region-locked Data Tier using CMEK and Row-Level Security, Cloud Armor WAF, SPIFFE mTLS via Service Mesh Proxy, signed receipts via Consent Cryptography Service, and tamper-resistant WORM tables and Cloud Audit Logs.
justifications.maintainability: High maintainability via modular containers and components with distinct responsibilities, such as separate EU National Gateway Adapter and US Pharmacy Network Adapter, decoupled SFU media pipelines, and event-driven integration through Event Broker Component.
justifications.portability: Containers run standardized runtimes (Go, Node.js, Python, Envoy) across target GCP regions europe-west3 and us-central1, but components exhibit tight coupling to proprietary GCP services (Cloud Armor, Cloud KMS, Memorystore, Cloud Audit Logs).

PERF-01.justification: The Mediasoup SFU and decoupled Signaling & Room Manager support low-latency WebRTC session negotiation. However, cluster autoscaling and port management for 5,000 concurrent media streams are not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: SFU media worker CPU and port allocation under high concurrent streams
tradeoffs: Decoupled signaling increases routing hops but enables horizontal scaling of media workers

PERF-02.justification: PyTorch inference runs on dedicated GPU pools behind FastAPI routing, handling ~14 requests/second easily. Audit logging is offloaded asynchronously via Pub/Sub, preventing inference latency bottlenecks.
sensitivity_points: GPU node pool provisioning and batch inference concurrency
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit publishing reduces request latency but delays immediate log consistency

AVAIL-01.justification: The Bandwidth Adaptability Controller explicitly manages dynamic Simulcast and SVC layers to downgrade video gracefully below 300 kbit/s. Consultation notes persist independently to Cloud SQL.
sensitivity_points: Threshold sensitivity of SVC/Simulcast layer degradation under rapid packet loss
tradeoffs: Dropping video resolution preserves audio quality and session continuity

AVAIL-02.justification: The platform configures only one US region (us-central1). A full regional outage cannot be recovered within 1 hour without migrating data to the EU or having an architected secondary US region.
sensitivity_points: Single US region dependency for strict US data residency constraints
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents cross-region failover to EU during US outages

MOD-01.justification: Prescription Router Component isolates downstream country adapters. Adding an EU country requires writing a new adapter implementation without affecting existing US or EU integration logic.
sensitivity_points: Standardized internal payload definition within Prescription Router
tradeoffs: Adapter encapsulation simplifies extensibility at the cost of per-adapter maintenance overhead

MOD-02.justification: Model execution is isolated in the inference core, and audit records capture model version and explainability outputs via Pub/Sub and WORM audit tables. Version rollback mechanisms in deployment pipelines are implied.
sensitivity_points: Inference metadata tagging and deterministic model version registration
tradeoffs: Capturing full explainability inputs ensures traceability but increases audit storage overhead

SEC-01.justification: Cross-region access is gated through Service Mesh Proxy, Consent Cryptography Service signing, and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security. Cloud Audit Logs capture all access requests immutably.
sensitivity_points: Cryptographic token verification and Row-Level Security rule evaluation
tradeoffs: Strict token-based cross-region checks add latency to cross-border clinical queries

SEC-02.justification: Consent revocation is processed by Revocation Manager, immediately persisted in PostgreSQL, cached in Memorystore Redis blocklists, and broadcast across services via Pub/Sub within seconds.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of Pub/Sub revocation events to regional cache blacklists
tradeoffs: Immediate distributed cache invalidation increases messaging traffic across containers
